hook
How can one small push lift a heavy car? Let's look inside a hydraulic lift.
parts
It has two pistons. A small one here, and a big one here.
parts
They're joined by a pipe, filled with oil.
secret
Here's the secret: oil can't be squeezed into a smaller space.
secret
So when you push the small piston down, the oil has to go somewhere.
secret
The pressure spreads equally through all the oil, pushing on every surface with the same strength.
force
The big piston has ten times more area, so it gets pushed up with ten times more force.
force
Push with ten kilograms, and it lifts one hundred kilograms!
catch
But there's a catch. Push the small piston down ten centimetres, and the big one rises only one centimetre.
catch
The same amount of oil just spreads out wider. You trade distance for force.
pump
That's why real lifts pump again and again. A one way valve stops the oil from flowing back.
uses
Hydraulics power car lifts, brakes, excavators, and even dentist chairs.
outro
One small push, one huge lift. That's hydraulics!
